title: [spec-gap][R-BB-020] bufferbloat_congestion.json multihop_latency pins 'bounded_e2e_delay', contradicting spec 'rather than promising an end-to-end delivery bound'
description: spec/appendix-bufferbloat.md:224-225 (Testing item 4): 'Multi-hop latency: Expire stale queued packets under load rather than promising an end-to-end delivery bound.' But the shared oracle test/vectors/bufferbloat_congestion.json scenario multihop_latency pins expected:'bounded_e2e_delay' — the opposite. The vector file self-describes as 'Literals from spec/appendix-bufferbloat.md Testing, not from queue implementations', so this is a stale literal from an earlier spec revision. The wrong expectation is pinned by two tests: rust/lichen-core/tests/bufferbloat_vectors.rs:125-127 (assert_eq!(case['expected'], 'bounded_e2e_delay')) and python/tests/test_bufferbloat_congestion_vectors.py:47. C lichen/tests/tx_queue does not consume the congestion file. Suggested placement: regenerate bufferbloat_congestion.json with a spec-conformant expectation (e.g. expected:'stale_expire_under_load', naming the expiry mechanism), update the two consumers to assert the new literal, and add a conformance test that actually exercises stale-packet expiry under offered load (tx_queue expiry vectors cover the mechanism; no test covers it under congestion). Same regeneration pass should fix stale 'B.2.x' section references: bufferbloat_congestion.json description cites 'Appendix B.5', no_silent_drops.json spec_section 'B.2.5', rust tests/bufferbloat_vectors.rs:4 'B.2', python lichen/timing/tx_queue.py docstring 'B.2/B.3', C tx_queue.h:70 'B.2.2' — the current spec uses named sections, not B.x numbering. Report-conflicting-fixture: fix vector + tests together against the spec text; do not edit the spec to match the fixture.
